title: Normalize SAML NameID/role prefixes and sweep KMS tombstones causing RBAC/authz drops and missing audit events
creator: Priya Narang
description: Summary: Several private-cluster customers reported repeated authorization failures and missing audit events after a control-plane upgrade window. Root cause analysis points to two related regressions: (1) SAML assertion claim normalization changed in the private control plane which caused client NameID and role claim prefixes (legacy 'urn:aws:role/' and customer-specific prefixes) to be treated as opaque strings instead of being normalized. This surface causes RBAC role lookup to fail for a subset of customers using federated role mapping. (2) Concurrently, a KMS envelope rotation path produced transient tombstoned DEK metadata in the store which caused Decrypt requests to surface 5xx errors for audit-log write paths, leading to dropped audit events under load. Together these caused sessions to be rejected intermittently and audit logs to omit entries for revoked sessions. Impact: customer-facing failures (API 401/403 spikes), alerts from SOC on missing audit trails, and at least two escalations with legal/regulatory risk for one customer. Scope: Privately hosted control planes across three customers in us-east and eu-west regions. Hosted/Dedicated unaffected.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a private control-plane build with the assertion-normalization change. 2) Configure SAML IdP to emit role claims with legacy prefix (e.g., 'urn:aws:role/12345'). 3) Trigger login/assume-role flows via the SDK. 4) Under a KMS rotation schedule (or simulated rotation), attempt operations that write audit events (token issuance, role binding changes). 5) Observe RBAC lookup failures in control plane logs and 5xx errors from KMS envelope unwraps leading to missing audit entries in the audit DB.
proposed_fix:
Short-term (hotpatch):
  - Revert the assertion-normalization transform in the private control-plane runtime and ship a micro-release that restores legacy prefix-aware matching. This avoids breaking customer role mappings.
  - Add a defensive retry and tombstone-filtering layer around KMS DEK unwrap: tombstoned metadata should be skipped and retried against previous envelope with exponential backoff. Roll this as a hotfix to control planes in the affected regions.
  - Backfill missing audit events where possible by replaying control-plane request logs into the audit pipeline (SRE + Compliance assistance).

  Long-term:
  - Implement idempotent claim normalization with a configurable compatibility mode per-tenant, and add an integration test that verifies role mapping compatibility with common IdPs.
  - Harden KMS envelope lifecycle: add stronger invariants and a GC sweep job that safely rewraps orphaned DEKs and marks tombstones for controlled cleanup.
  - Add an end-to-end e2e test simulating KMS rotation and audit write contention to prevent regressions.
rollback_plan: If hotpatch causes regressions, revert the release to the previous known-good control-plane binary for the affected clusters using the standard rollback job. For KMS unwrap changes, disable the new tombstone-filtering path through runtime feature flag and revert the config change. Maintain an open channel with customer SREs during rollback.
